request.project_task: Build a travel expense submission and approval workflow.
request.project_goal: Reduce manual checking of employee expense claims.
request.project_description: An employee submits receipts; a manager reviews policy exceptions and finance reimburses approved claims.

functional_requirements.text: An employee creates an expense claim with trip details.

atoms.text: An employee creates an expense claim with trip details.

functional_requirements.text: The employee attaches receipts to expense items.

atoms.text: The employee attaches receipts to expense items.

functional_requirements.text: The system flags items above policy limits.

atoms.text: The system flags items above policy limits.

functional_requirements.text: A manager approves or rejects the claim.

atoms.text: A manager approves or rejects the claim.

functional_requirements.text: Finance records reimbursement for an approved claim.

atoms.text: Finance records reimbursement for an approved claim.

non_functional_requirements.text: Receipt files must be encrypted at rest.
All approval decisions must be auditable.

actors.name: Employee
actors.description: A staff member who incurs travel expenses and submits claims for reimbursement.

actors.name: Manager
actors.description: A person responsible for reviewing and approving or rejecting employee expense claims.

actors.name: Finance Officer
actors.description: A person responsible for recording reimbursement of approved claims.

actors.name: System
actors.description: The automated travel claims system that enforces policy and stores data.

use_cases.name: Submit Travel Expense Claim
use_cases.goal: Employee creates and submits a travel expense claim with trip details and receipts.
use_cases.trigger: Employee decides to submit a travel expense claim.

preconditions.text: Employee is authenticated and authorized to create expense claims.

success_postconditions.text: Expense claim is created and submitted with trip details and attached receipts.

failure_postconditions.text: Expense claim is not submitted; employee is notified of the failure.

main_success_scenario.name: Employee submits a complete expense claim

steps.action: Employee initiates a new expense claim and enters trip details.
steps.expected_result: System creates a draft expense claim with trip details.

steps.action: Employee adds expense items and attaches receipts to each item.
steps.expected_result: Receipts are attached to expense items.

steps.action: System flags any expense items that exceed policy limits.
steps.expected_result: Items above policy limits are flagged for review.
Claim is submitted and routed to the manager for approval.

steps.action: Employee attempts to attach a receipt but the upload fails.
steps.expected_result: System displays an error and does not attach the receipt.

steps.action: Employee retries attaching the receipt or removes the item.
steps.expected_result: Employee can proceed with valid receipts or remove the item.

user_stories.capability: create an expense claim with trip details and attach receipts
user_stories.benefit: I can submit my travel expenses for reimbursement.

system_stories.system_action: Flag expense items above policy limits
system_stories.responsibility: Enforce policy limits and mark items for manager review.

use_cases.human_readable_text:
Use Case: UC-001 — Submit Travel Expense Claim
Goal: Employee creates and submits a travel expense claim with trip details and receipts.
Primary actor: ACT-001
Trigger: Employee decides to submit a travel expense claim.
Preconditions:
  - PRE-UC001-001: Employee is authenticated and authorized to create expense claims.
Main success scenario:
  1. [STEP-UC001-001] Employee initiates a new expense claim and enters trip details.
  2. [STEP-UC001-002] Employee adds expense items and attaches receipts to each item.
  3. [STEP-UC001-003] System flags any expense items that exceed policy limits.
  4. [STEP-UC001-004] Employee submits the expense claim.
Exception scenarios:
  - SCN-UC001-EXC-001: Receipt attachment fails
Source FRs: FR-001, FR-002, FR-003

use_cases.name: Review and Decide on Expense Claim
use_cases.goal: Manager reviews a submitted expense claim and approves or rejects it.
use_cases.trigger: A submitted expense claim is routed to the manager for approval.

preconditions.text: Manager is authenticated and authorized to approve expense claims.
An expense claim has been submitted and is pending approval.

success_postconditions.text: Claim is approved or rejected, and the decision is recorded.

failure_postconditions.text: Claim remains pending; manager is notified of the failure.

steps.action: Manager opens the submitted expense claim for review.
steps.expected_result: System displays claim details, receipts, and flagged policy exceptions.

steps.action: Manager reviews the claim and decides to approve it.
steps.expected_result: System records the approval decision and updates claim status.

steps.action: Manager reviews the claim and decides to reject it.
steps.expected_result: System records the rejection decision and updates claim status.

user_stories.capability: review and approve or reject expense claims
user_stories.benefit: I can ensure policy compliance and control expenses.

system_stories.system_action: Record approval or rejection decision with audit trail
system_stories.responsibility: Maintain an auditable record of all approval decisions.

use_cases.human_readable_text:
Use Case: UC-002 — Review and Decide on Expense Claim
Goal: Manager reviews a submitted expense claim and approves or rejects it.
Primary actor: ACT-002
Trigger: A submitted expense claim is routed to the manager for approval.
Preconditions:
  - PRE-UC002-001: Manager is authenticated and authorized to approve expense claims.
  - PRE-UC002-002: An expense claim has been submitted and is pending approval.
Main success scenario:
  1. [STEP-UC002-001] Manager opens the submitted expense claim for review.
  2. [STEP-UC002-002] Manager reviews the claim and decides to approve it.
Alternative scenarios:
  - SCN-UC002-ALT-001: Manager rejects a claim
Source FRs: FR-004

use_cases.name: Record Reimbursement
use_cases.goal: Finance records reimbursement for an approved expense claim.
use_cases.trigger: An expense claim has been approved and is ready for reimbursement.

preconditions.text: Finance officer is authenticated and authorized to record reimbursements.
An expense claim has been approved by a manager.

success_postconditions.text: Reimbursement is recorded for the approved claim.

failure_postconditions.text: Reimbursement is not recorded; finance officer is notified of the failure.

steps.action: Finance officer opens the approved expense claim.
Finance officer records the reimbursement for the claim.
steps.expected_result: System records reimbursement and updates claim status.

user_stories.benefit: I can ensure employees are reimbursed accurately.

system_stories.system_action: Record reimbursement details and update claim status

use_cases.human_readable_text:
Use Case: UC-003 — Record Reimbursement
Goal: Finance records reimbursement for an approved expense claim.
Primary actor: ACT-003
Trigger: An expense claim has been approved and is ready for reimbursement.
Preconditions:
  - PRE-UC003-001: Finance officer is authenticated and authorized to record reimbursements.
  - PRE-UC003-002: An expense claim has been approved by a manager.
Main success scenario:
  1. [STEP-UC003-001] Finance officer opens the approved expense claim.
  2. [STEP-UC003-002] Finance officer records the reimbursement for the claim.
Source FRs: FR-005

issues.message: Edge ADE-UC001-001 must link to UC step(s) or be marked unsupported

The exception scenario 'Receipt attachment fails' is modeled as a decision immediately after the main step 'Add expense items and attach receipts'. This is a reasonable equivalent control-flow decomposition of the exception, but it slightly alters the main-flow ordering by inserting the exception check before the policy-limit flagging step. No UC step is omitted or contradicted, so this is non-blocking.

The merge node 'Continue with valid receipts' is traced to STEP-UC001-006, which is an exception-scenario step. This is acceptable as a rejoining construct, but the trace could be clearer by also referencing the main-flow step it rejoins.

details.summary: The activity diagram preserves all main-success steps (STEP-UC001-001 through STEP-UC001-004) and both exception steps (STEP-UC001-005, STEP-UC001-006). No UC step is omitted or contradicted, and no unsupported business action is introduced. The exception handling is modeled as an equivalent control-flow decomposition. No evidence-grounded blocking issue remains; accept.
